correctness.rationale: For stable real diagonal A=diag(a,d), a!=d, the exact series give W=[[px,rsqrt(x(1-x))],[rsqrt(x(1-x)),q(1-x)]], where p=(1-a^2)^-1, q=(1-d^2)^-1, r=(1-ad)^-1. The determinant is (pq-r^2)x(1-x)>0 interior. Since tr(W)^2/det(W)=kappa+1/kappa+2 is monotone in kappa>=1, the ratio (q+(p-q)x)^2/[x(1-x)] has its unique global minimum at x=q/(p+q), with boundary divergence. Optimal equal diagonal energies yield rho=r/sqrt(pq), kappa=(1+rho)/(1-rho)=coth^2(|atanh(a)-atanh(d)|/2). Independently repeated four rational pair checks and the a=0,d=3/5 example with W=[[25,20],[20,25]]/41 and kappa=9; finite tests are not the proof.
